The raised total ends with a single low turn and exit compatible with 2, not a two-lobed 3. The author's sum of three (quantity-1) terms would arithmetically end in -3, but the written -2 is retained. The final face total has -1.

Below the vertex, a large flagged 1 with a horizontal foot lies by the lower-left branch, and a separate large looped 9 lies by the lower-right branch. Their placements on the two sides of the vertex are distinct; H combines the lower pair into 19. The flagged first digit of the separate 15 at the leftmost vertex was compared with this large 1 and supports C/H 15.

### Still unresolved

- cancelled acronym in first display: `\deleted{\unsure{\mathrm{F}}\mathrm{MD}}` — The extra initial form is partly covered; MD is legible.
- graph tuple, old origin glyph: `\deleted{\unsure{g}}` — Dense overhatching hides most of its strokes.
- graph tuple, replacement above the cancelled glyph: `\inserted{\unsure{o|\sigma}}` — A small oval has a conspicuous rightward upper stroke; this can be an extended o closure or sigma. The label is not regularized by mathematical expectation.
- graph tuple, cancelled sign before gamma: `\deleted{\unsure{)}}` — The outline is bracket-like, but internal strokes are obscured.
- S formula, cancelled sign after X: `\deleted{\unsure{)|,}}` — The sign is tall and curved; cancellation prevents certainty.
- pair (C, omega), cancelled glyph: `\deleted{\unsure{\xi}}` — Not all old strokes survive separately from the cancellation.
- C membership clause, cancelled draft: `\deleted{\unsure{$\in A$|est un}}` — A is visible, but low remaining strokes admit a verbal reading.
- origin-map label: `\deleted{\unsure{O}}\inserted{o}` — The upper label cluster contains several overwritten loops whose individual scope is not secure.
- cancelled formula before contient cette rive: `\deleted{$\unsure{R\subset\widetilde R}$}` — The cancellation hides most of the relation and some of the right-hand symbol.
- old glyph below the last weight-map label: `\deleted{\unsure{\rho}}` — The descending stroke is repeatedly overdrawn; rho is a tentative recovery only.
- punctuation after 0-isomorphisme: `\deleted{\unsure{)|?}}` — Central cancellation strokes prevent recovery of the whole sign.

### Still unresolved

- opening line: `somme` — The final low cursive stroke does not separate a terminal s securely; the singular is favoured only as the closer stroke reading.
- first display, cancelled group after X: `\deleted{\unsure{est}}` — Several overlapping strikes obscure the individual letters.
- margin note, cancelled formula: `\deleted{\unsure{=1-\chi(\Gamma)}}` — The lower cancelled line has several surviving symbols, but overstriking and the live replacement prevent firm segmentation.
- item a), cancelled notation: `\deleted{\unsure{S_*\mathcal T_{\mathrm{top}}}}` — Multiple diagonal cancellations cross the principal symbols.
- last paragraph, old participle: `\deleted{\unsure{Déterminé}}` — Inserted letters and a cancellation line lie over the word.
- last paragraph, upper replacement: `\deleted{\inserted{caractérisé}}` — The long strike intersects the lower part of the inserted word, but cancellation scope is ambiguous.
- last paragraph, old noun phrase: `\deleted{\unsure{le genre}}` — The cancellation hides part of the genre group.
- last paragraph, Le cas d'une placement: `\inserted{Le cas d'une}` — Its position above the old cancelled beginning suggests replacement; the page also permits a linear layout reading.
- first diagram, exponent of final vector A: `\sigma` — The superscript touches the vector accent; its outline is not sufficient to decide sigma against a star in isolation. The local involution notation favours sigma without eliminating the visual doubt.

### Still unresolved

- After désigne: `l'\unsure{ens|un} des` — The low joined strokes favour ens but do not decisively separate its three letters.
- Four map-name occurrences: `\unsure{p|\rho}` — The small bowl and descending stem favour p relative to the opening prose rho, but this cursive form also admits rho; the doubt is retained consistently.
- Cancelled identity subscript: `\operatorname{id}_{\unsure{R_a|R}}` — The small terminal loop could be a distinct a or the end of the crowded R.
- Old word before inserted remplacée: `\unsure{complétée}` — Two crossing strokes cover the middle of the old word. Initial c and the long p/l region remain compatible with complétée.
- Cancelled application after à savoir: `\unsure{application}` — The two p descenders and tall l can be seen, but the stroke hides several middle letters.
- Cancelled upper word after une: `\unsure{triple|famille}` — The upper une is left of the short cancellation and remains live. The upper cancelled word has a tall initial t-like stroke, a compact r/i region, a descending p-like stroke and a final tall loop, favouring triple; famille remains an alternative because the lower application strokes overlap it. The later large famille is uncrossed. The first placement of that final word is retained; the cropped geometry does not establish that the entire later word is an interlinear insertion.
- Cancelled phrase and lower-left attachment: `\deleted{\unsure{donné d'une permutation}} \unsure{\deleted{de}|deux}` — The live text has d’ensembles and the inverted-A quantifier. The double quotation strokes bracket orientations, not de a. The heavily struck intervening wording retains visible p/t fragments but cannot be read with a secure word count. The small lower-left de-like group lies near the next baseline; its attachment as cancelled de versus a live deux-like group remains doubtful and is marked in place. Ens versus un also remains open.
- Cancelled tail after R to A: `\unsure{conj. à}` — The very faint tail after R to A is crossed; neither all letters nor the abbreviation point can be isolated securely.
- Cancelled word after et before injection: `\unsure{d'autre|relie à}` — The first cancelled words remain crossed through their centres; d’autre versus relie à and the first une-like group are uncertain. An additional small residual group precedes the second une; bi. is a possible reading, not a resolved abbreviation. Application is readable. The final word has the j descender, t, dotted i and on ending of injection, with a separate underline; it is not injective. The old map has a left hook and a pointed right arrowhead.
- First une-like run in cancelled injection phrase: `\unsure{une}` — A shallow three-stroke run is visible but partly lies on the cancellation.
- Remaining cancelled injection phrase and segmentation: `\unsure{\illegible{1}|bi.} une application \uline{injection}` — The first cancelled words remain crossed through their centres; d’autre versus relie à and the first une-like group are uncertain. An additional small residual group precedes the second une; bi. is a possible reading, not a resolved abbreviation. Application is readable. The final word has the j descender, t, dotted i and on ending of injection, with a separate underline; it is not injective. The old map has a left hook and a pointed right arrowhead.

### Still unresolved

- Cancelled word under à repères: `\unsure{enrichi}` — The heavy overlapping strokes obscure the letter bodies; the C doubt is retained.
- Cancelled symbol between first R and subset: `\unsure{\mathbb D_\infty|D_\infty}` — The contour is compatible with D but the crossing obscures whether its upright was doubled.
- Initial diagram, downward-arrow label: `\unsure{o|\sigma}` — The subset is a separate curved inclusion sign, and the loop on vector A has its sigma label. The old D-infinity is crossed so that single/double stem remains uncertain. The downward-arrow label has a closed oval with a short upper-right extension: o versus sigma is not fully separable and is now explicit. The cursive l, both sigma indices, plus, gamma and double-stem N agree.
- Inserted parenthesis, before valeurs: `\unsure{à|:}` — The small mark before valeurs has an upper dot/stroke and a compact lower mark; it can be the author’s reduced à or colon, so both remain explicit. The parenthetical has et non seulement, le foncteur, dans and two closing parentheses. There is no extra dot in Grbipond; line-break differences alone are not a reading change.

### Still unresolved

- Cancelled quotient after the first live group: `\deleted{\unsure{\mathbb Z/r(a)|\mathbb Z(\omega(a))}}` — The live quotient has the same short shoulder r as the clearer later r(a) occurrences, not a newly introduced nu. Under the cancellation a Z-like group and a long division-like stroke favour the old quotient Z/r(a), but the following rounded group also admits the independent Z(omega(a)) reading. Both old candidates remain doubtful. The parenthetical definition begins above the cancelled group and is a raised replacement; its insertion state is now recorded. Its doubled Z diagonals, wedge, omega(a) and brace-enclosed plus/minus 1 are visible.
- Whole inserted multiplier identity: `$r''(a)$ \inserted{$=\unsure{d_a|d(a)}r(a)$}` — The a is lowered below d, while a nearby curved stroke may belong to an opening parenthesis. Later clear d(a) occurrences do not override this local ambiguity.
- Source/target separator in contraction and extension lines: `\unsure{à|:}` — Both compact marks have a separate upper point/stroke and small lower body, leaving the letter versus punctuation distinction unresolved.

### Still unresolved

- Heading, cancelled preposition: `\deleted{\unsure{de|des}}` — The old d-like loop and ascender are covered by several overstrikes. The terminal dark hooked mass may include s, so de remains primary but des is added as an explicit alternative. Neither is resolved.
- Upper paragraph, cancelled edge adjective: `\deleted{\unsure{ord.|sol.}}` — The old run is short: an oval entry, angular joined middle, one looped ascender and a separate small point. It does not expose the long -inaires continuation required for ordinaires. Ord. is preferred provisionally, with the independent sol. as an alternative. The replacement has one tall l, short i and accented e-like ending, favouring liees over libres. The closing parenthesis meets the strike at its bottom, but the curve itself is not clearly cancelled.
- First long cancelled line, final group: `\unsure{à}` — The old opening has a large I, a small c and short i, then the low e/n/c/o/r/e run ending before a comma: Ici encore, not Les or Je. Pour has a descending p and un has its two low joins. At the far end two small surviving upper traces include an a-like body and a raised accent-like stroke, now tentatively a-grave rather than wholly illegible. The whole abandoned line is cancelled.
- Marked case, cancelled tail: `\unsure{lieu de marquer|bel et bien}` — In the cancelled tail the first tall/short joins and the following ascender are more compatible with lieu de, followed by a low marquer-like run, than with the previous bel et bien/tel et un alternatives; lieu de marquer is now a doubtful leading reading. The small a after the descending y falls low, directly above the next Sigma, and is part of il y a rather than a cc index. The replacement marque remains live despite its q descender crossing the lower strike. The raised verbal replacement is kept separately from the continuing live i.e. formula: the image does not establish that the latter was itself an added revision. Phi keeps its oval/stem form. After the next dash the descending first letter and short u/i support qui, not sauf. The terminal s in choses remains.
- Parenthesis after fini: `\unsure{en près}` — The faint first group has a small e-like entry and low n run. The second has p, a short r-like middle, accented e-like body and final s; there is no tall l for plus. En pres remains doubtful, while the plus alternative is dropped. The clipped descender does not justify supplying a longer phrase.
- Verb after peut se: `\unsure{réverser|inverser}` — The raised initial mark can be an accent or i dot, and the initial connected group remains ambiguous.
- Closing quote ticks after gommer: `\unsure{''|'}` — The quoted verbs, contracter, un point and decouper agree. The closing mark after gommer is a small joined stroke whose individual ticks cannot be counted securely, so one/two closing ticks are now uncertain. After the e of the first i.e there is no separate terminal point; only its exit stroke is present. The intervening point and dotted i are retained.

### Still unresolved

- Item 1, first raised circle group: `\inserted{\unsure{$C_a$|$C_0$}}` — The first item digit has an ascending diagonal, a right upright and a transverse stroke, giving a 4-like form; 1 remains possible under retracing and is not imposed by the sequence. The first raised circle symbol has a capital open C and a low oval, permitting a or 0 as index. The second raised group has a tall loop and reduced es-like ending, so les/C_a remains unresolved. The cancelled sur un cercle is not promoted to certainty.
- Item 1, second raised group: `\inserted{\unsure{les|$C_a$}}` — Tall left and compressed right strokes remain compatible with either reading; the leader fixes the attachment but not the letters.
- Item 1, cancelled sur un cercle: `\deleted{\unsure{sur un cercle}}` — The strike obscures enough joins that every letter cannot be certified.
- Item 1, article after suppression: `\unsure{d'une|de la}` — The apostrophe-like stroke and u/n humps favour d’une, but overwritten earlier strokes and exact addition state cannot be separated.
- Item 1, cancelled de R continuation: `\deleted{\unsure{de $R$ se trouvant dans une partie}}` — Dans is favoured by its d-ascender, but the whole cancellation still hides other letters.
- Item 2, isolated glyph beside divisor relation: `\unsure{2|?}` — It is definite dark ink, but its loop, descending stroke and lower foot do not establish its function.
- Margin to item 2, r_a condition: `$r_a\unsure{\ge|>}1$` — The additional short bars merge with the retraced > outline.
- Margin to item 2, crossed low word: `\deleted{\unsure{anodin}}` — The horizontal cancellation masks central cursive joins; no argument from the classification is used to supply them.
- Margin to item 2, first divisor relation: `$r'_a\unsure{\mid|\ne}r_a$ et $r'_a\ne r_a$` — A long heavy stroke crosses shorter bars. The later clear not-equal and the identity d_a=r_a/r′_a do not settle the overwritten sign.
- Item 3, whole quotient pair: `$\mathbb Z_a/r_a\mathbb Z_a$ à $\mathbb Z/\unsure{d|d_a}r_a\mathbb Z$` — The article before groupes has a looped d and low es run; the noun has g and p descenders followed by es, supporting des groupes. The target numerator is a doubled Z without a separate low a. The multiplier d has a long foot but no securely separate subscript; d/d_a is retained with unindexed d first. The source quotient has both a indices. The final target Z has no lower a, and the terminal comma is distinct.
- Margin to item 3, underline extent: `\uline{affaiblissement de}\quad structure \uline{faible}` — Only a short pale trace lies near structure; the full continuous underline of C is not visible.
- Footnote, extra group before exclure: `\unsure{$=$|\deleted{ou}}` — The short straight upper bar and separate wavy lower stroke favour equals. Main reader reports the same form in 063 same_temps, which reader_b did not inspect; the local alternative is retained.
- First main item number: `$\unsure{4^\circ|1^\circ}$)` — The first item digit has an ascending diagonal, a right upright and a transverse stroke, giving a 4-like form; 1 remains possible under retracing and is not imposed by the sequence. The first raised circle symbol has a capital open C and a low oval, permitting a or 0 as index. The second raised group has a tall loop and reduced es-like ending, so les/C_a remains unresolved. The cancelled sur un cercle is not promoted to certainty.
- Margin to item 2, grammatical endings: `\unsure{de|des} \unsure{structure|structures} \unsure{faible|faibles}` — The whole rotated margin was viewed. The terminal strokes of de/structure/faible can contain small plural s strokes, so these endings are now explicitly doubtful without being supplied from grammar. The r_a condition ends in a tall hooked 1, not a closed oval 0. The overworked relation still permits greater-or-equal/greater. The first lower relation is heavily overwritten; its divides/not-equal alternatives remain. The later not-equal and the ratio formula are clear. The old crossed word retains its anodin doubt. The open upper/right boundary is retained once.
- Item 3, replacement operation name: `\unsure{-gommage|dégommage}` — The canonical crop and D07 detail show a short horizontal stroke before a looped descending g, then the low o/mm/a sequence and the second g descender. No separate Surmar- sequence is exposed. The primary heading is now -gommage, with degommage retained as an alternative because the small opening strokes are compressed. The numeral has two curved lobes supporting 3. Extension des is crossed below the added heading.
- Margin to item 3, grammatical endings: `\unsure{de|des} \unsure{structure|structures} \unsure{faible|faibles}` — The open top/right boundary and separate lower formula were viewed. The final hooks can be singular word exits or plural s, so de/des, structure/structures and faible/faibles are explicitly uncertain. The lower sign is a clear crossed equals followed by oval 0. The underline below faible is distinct; the faint trace below structure is not extended into a continuous underline.
- Articles in items 4 and 5: `\unsure{de|du}` — Both numerals are circled and one left brace joins the two lines. The short articles have reduced e/u bowls, so de remains first with du as alternative. The same-box index detail shows one looped cursive l directly after A in item 5, with no independent 0 or comma: A_l. Item 4 has a separate small oval 0. The circled 4 and 5 are not duplicated in the margin.
- Cancelled adjective before reversible: `\deleted{\unsure{faiblement|faible}}` — Under the long cancellation, faible is followed by further low m/e/n/t-like strokes, so faiblement is now first while faible remains an alternative because the strike covers the joins. After reversible two short bars precede a low a/n/o run, tall d, dotted i and final n: anodin. There are no separate a/en condition words. The lower inequality has its additional bar and ends in 1 plus a separate point. The bottom separator belongs to the next margin and is represented there once.
- Word after item 7 opening parenthesis: `\unsure{avec}` — The canonical box, D11 and the opening detail were viewed. Between the opening parenthesis and a,a-prime there is faint compressed ink; it is not blank, but the v/e/c joins formerly read avec are not individually secure, so avec is retained under doubt. The pair uses the same open handwritten a forms as the nearby a indices. A_l has one cursive l. The raised equality has a curved leader returning before the closing parenthesis; that leader is not an additional parenthesis. The final product is an unbarred wedge.
- Margin to item 7 inequality: `\unsure{\ge|>}` — The equality of the two r parameters and the prime on the second index are visible. The overworked greater sign has a lower short bar, but its final state still permits greater as an alternative. The next line has two short equals bars and the readable a-n-o-d-i-n sequence with tall d, not a/en condition. The upper separator is retained once.

There is no de after the right circulaire: the next line begins with the bracket. The intervening sign has a curved upper stroke and a lower bar; the diagonal continues far beyond it as a global stroke, so the underlying sign is simeq. A dark terminal point follows the right bracket; no colon follows the group quotient. Cancellation scope is retained as probable but explicitly uncertain.; crops/148_scan067_second_B06.png (1480, 705, 2370, 1058) | low |

The outer contour and several wrapping runs are irregular, partly disconnected and retraced; the second tracing preserves those visible ends rather than completing smooth ellipses. The local circles have separate dark and broken sectors and clear arrows at 0 and 1. No distinct infinity arrowhead is forced from its short angular trace. The older connectivity remains qualified.
- Upper right sommets ending: `\unsure{sommets|sommet}` — The counts and complete formulas were viewed. The upper right word has a compressed exit, leaving sommets/sommet open, but d'ordre and the three raised prime marks are clear. In the overworked edge word a long g-like descender survives, so the older bigones layer cannot be discarded in favour of a wholly clear aretes. The cancelled old sum remains doubtful. The raised total ends with a single low turn and exit compatible with 2, not a two-lobed 3. The author's sum of three (quantity-1) terms would arithmetically end in -3, but the written -2 is retained. The final face total has -1.
- Small triangle, third left-side label: `\unsure{b_3}` — The accepted B13 final tracing already leaves this third left-side b_3 label explicitly doubtful. This entry maps that existing local letter/index uncertainty individually; it is separate from the inter-hole b_3^1 alternative and does not introduce a new ink decision. Existing evidence: crops/148_scan067_second_B13.png.

Examples include the break below-left of the central zero at approximately (899,588), the separate endpoints near (812,425) in the upper-left fan, and breaks in the right-hand return strokes near (1215,578). C replaces these with ten smooth closed cycles, sixteen regular ellipses and twelve separately placed generic arrows. The two upper doubtful labels lie inside the small loops and are rotated; the left doubtful infinity is low and oblique within its loop, and the doubtful 1 lies on the lower-left side of the small upper-central loop. The central 0, the 1 at i, the infinity at j and the lower infinity at l lie to the left of their junctions. The lower-right 1 and infinity sit within their loops. All sixteen label values were read separately; four obscured values remain doubtful, with b now leading 0 and the local alternatives recorded individually. This row counts placement, not the separate value correction at b. H mentions the three kinds of label but provides no individual mapping or placements.; crops/148_scan069_whole_graph.png (380, 75, 1560, 1250) | high |

C supplies a ninth extended smooth cycle starting at (900,467); its long segment follows the grey doubled c--f pencil trace, where left_inner shows no independent long red curve. H count eight agrees with the ink, but its prose does not reproduce the drawing. The actual red loops, local thickened projections, dots and small openings replace C regular ellipses and generic arrows. | The graph has a six-sided cycle, two lower stems, a lower-left fork, six exterior rays and one loop attached to the lower-right vertex. Eight dark vertices and twenty-three numerical annotations were read individually. The three enclosures surround 1, 2 and 3 at their actual positions; the last enclosure has a small upper-right opening. The rightward ray has an irregular thickening and pointed end, preserved as a local outline. C regularizes these enclosure/ray shapes. H gives only a compressed verbal description and number list, without the complete incidence-to-weight mapping. The source values otherwise agree with C, including 15, 17 and the repeated 3, 4 and 5 labels. The independent audit leaves the retraced weight at the left vertex doubtful as 15/25; its leading value remains 15. This added uncertainty is not another witness-change row.; crops/148_scan072_right_graph.png (1473, 637, 2154, 1125) | medium |
